Occurrences.Kwic: 師聞得陞堂云：要會臨濟賓主句，問取堂中二禪客
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Linji, complete unit: after hearing two fellow students exchange lines, Linji Yixuan mounts the hall and tells the assembly to ask the two Chan visitors if they want to understand Linji's guest-and-host phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃曰：適來禪客出眾禮拜，各以無量珍寶布施大眾。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Foyin Liaoyuan hall address: Foyin directly says that the Chan visitors who just came forward and bowed have distributed immeasurable treasures and emitted light, then challenges the assembly to see it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 而今敢問諸禪客，吐得狐涎盡也無
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linked Pearls Collection, wild-fox verse sequence: an unnamed capping-verse author asks the Chan visitors whether all fox drool has been spat out. Baizhang Huaihai is the case source, not this verse's utterer.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The headword occurs in one of the anthology's successive unattributed verses on Baizhang's wild-fox case, asking Chan visitors whether they have spat out all fox drool.

Occurrences.Kwic: 禪月貫休禪月貫休禪師有詩曰：禪客相逢祇彈指，此心能有幾人知？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Forest of the Chan Mirror explicitly quotes a poem by Chanyue Guanxiu: 'When Chan visitors meet, they only snap a finger.' Guanxiu is the named poet-monk utterer; the later masters are commentators.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 禪月貫休禪師有詩曰 explicitly attributes the quoted line 禪客相逢祇彈指 to the poet-monk Guanxiu; later masters' questions and substitutes are separate turns.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師謂曰：禪客，我不會禪，並無一法可示於人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Dazhu Huihai biography: as visitors increasingly gather, Dazhu directly addresses them as Chan visitors and says he neither understands Chan nor has a single teaching to show them.

Complete Nanyang Huizhong examination: the narrator labels the unnamed Chan visitor as the object of Nanyang's question. Nanyang is the named questioner; neither speaker utters the title inside quoted speech.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 師問禪客 is a narrator-owned dialogue cue identifying Nanyang Huizhong's unnamed visitor; Nanyang asks where he came from, and the visitor answers from the south.

Occurrences.Kwic: 而今賣與諸禪客，文契分明要也無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Luohan Xinglin hall address: the named but not-yet-rostered master lifts a cat and says he now sells it to the Chan visitors with a clear deed.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The section header names Luohan Xinglin; 上堂 and 師提起示眾曰 mark his direct speech offering the cat for sale to the Chan visitors.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂拈云：若要清風再復，頭角重生，請諸禪客下一轉語。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete rhinoceros-fan unit in Yanguan Qi'an's section: after the preserved substitutes, Yanguan raises the case, asks the Chan visitors for a turning phrase, then tests a monk's answer and shouts.

Senses.Explanation: A Chan visitor is a monastic participant addressed or identified within the public life of a master's community. Linji points the hall toward two such visitors after their exchange; Foyin interprets visitors' bows before the assembly; Dazhu addresses arriving students by the title; Nanyang examines one from the south; and Yanguan challenges the visitors to supply a turning phrase. Verse writers also address this audience. The term therefore marks an active interview participant or visiting student, not simply any traveler.
